title: After 31 Years, This Legendary Sci-Fi Anime Movie Still Has No Worthy Competition
content:
During a career spanning over forty years, Mamoru Oshii became a pioneering anime director and filmmaker, best known for his incredible work in the Ghost in the Shell franchise. While the legendary director has been a part of the industry since the 1980s, he got his global breakthrough thanks to the Ghost in the Shell film in 1995. The film not only became a massive hit in Japan, but it made Oshii globally renowned after catching the attention of fans in the United States and Europe. Oshii is particularly famous for his distinctive , philosophy-oriented storytelling, along with artistic style, sometimes even prioritizing visuals over the plot.

Before his greatest sci-fi movie, he made his directorial debut in 1983 with the Urusei Yatsura: Only You film, and then released another film of the franchise in the following year. Ghost in the Shell premiered in Japan on November 18th, 1995, exactly 31 years ago. It’s safe to say that the film has had no worthy competition over the decades. This also applies to the anime remake by Science SARU , which was one of the biggest hits of the year. While the remake was a more faithful adaptation of the acclaimed manga by Masamune Shirow, Oshii took liberties in his storytelling, making it stand out from other anime.

Ghost in the Shell Movie Can’t Be Recreated Today

Due to the advancement in technology, modern animation has changed significantly over the years. Unlike the animation from a few decades ago, animators rely mostly on a blend of traditional hand-drawn animation with digital techniques, primarily using CGI for lighting, coloring, backgrounds, and motion. This allows the animators to include more details in each frame, creating a unique sense of depth and aesthetic appeal. However, while modern animation has its perks, it’s evident that modern technology can’t create such intricate details as seen in the older anime , especially something as artistic as Ghost in the Shell .

The film is a pioneer of new animation techniques, known for its stunning visuals through the use of a blend of traditional cel animation with early computer-generated imagery. The anime industry largely moved from traditional cel animation to digital pipelines in the early 2000s, completely changing the art style and the grainy visuals that fans appreciate from the 1990s anime even now. Not to mention that Ghost in the Shell is one of those rare cases where changes from the manga can be seen as a more intriguing method of storytelling, especially if you realize what kind of vibe Oshii was going for.

Oshii’s adaptation took a much darker tone than the original manga, especially with the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi. Although she is more cheerful in the manga, her personality in the movie suited the intense themes in the movie, especially considering its futuristic setting. It wasn’t just her, but the overall manga had a much more cheerful and warm vibe, all the while portraying the problems within the futuristic society.

Do you think any modern sci-fi anime has come close to matching Ghost in the Shell ? What makes this legendary sci-fi movie so timeless? Share your thoughts in the comments!

title: Classroom of the Elite Season 5 Announces 2027 Premiere Date
content:
It was announced at the MF Bunko J Autumn School Festival event that Classroom of the Elite Season 5 is set to premiere in 2027. A teaser visual and trailer were also released. Season 5 was officially announced immediately after the fourth season’s finale premiered.

The anime is an adaptation of Shogo Kinugasa’s Classroom of the Elite light novels. The first season premiered in 2017 and had 12 episodes. Season 2 was announced in March 2022, and it ran for 13 episodes in the Summer 2022 anime season. Season 3 was delayed from its original schedule and ended up premiering in January 2024, also getting a total of 13 episodes. Season 4 aired from April to June 2026.

Crunchyroll is streaming the anime, and they describe the story: Kiyotaka Ayanokoji has just enrolled at Tokyo Koudo Ikusei Senior High School, where it’s said that 100% of students go on to college or find employment. But he ends up in Class 1-D, which is full of all the school’s problem children. What’s more, every month, the school awards students points with a cash value of 100,000 yen, and the classes employ a laissez-faire policy in which talking, sleeping, and even sabotage are permitted during class. One month later, Ayanokoji, Horikita, and the students of Class D learn the truth of the system in place within their school…

title: 'Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 5th Season: 2-nensei-hen 2 Gakki' Airs in 2027
content:
The MF Bunko J Autumn School Festival 2026 revealed cast members, main staff, and a teaser visual (pictured) for Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 5th Season: 2-nensei-hen 2 Gakki ( Classroom of the Elite 5th Season: Second Year, Second Semester ) on Sunday. The first part of the fifth season adapting Shougo Kinugasa 's 2-nensei-hen ( Year 2 ) sequel light novel will premiere in 2027.

Cast Kiyotaka Ayanokouji: Shouya Chiba ( 86 ) Suzune Horikita: Akari Kitou ( Mato Seihei no Slave ) Kei Karuizawa: Ayana Taketatsu ( Kanojo mo Kanojo ) Kikyou Kushida: Yurika Kubo ( Haite Kudasai, Takamine-san ) Kakeru Ryuuen: Masaaki Mizunaka ( Tsue to Tsurugi no Wistoria ) Honami Ichinose: Nao Touyama ( Bokutachi no Remake ) Arisu Sakayanagi: Rina Hidaka ( Kage no Jitsuryokusha ni Naritakute! ) Tsubasa Nanase: Minako Satou ( Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun ) Kazuomi Housen: Hiroya Egashira ( Ragna Crimson ) Ichika Amasawa: Momoko Seto ( Uma Musume: Cinderella Gray ) Takuya Yagami: Shinnosuke Tokudome ( Kijin Gentoushou ) Sakurako Tsubaki: Iori Saeki ( Shokei Shoujo no Virgin Road ) Riku Utomiya: Shougo Sakata ( Chiyu Mahou no Machigatta Tsukaikata ) Miyabi Nagumo: Souma Saitou ( Yuukoku no Moriarty )

Staff Director: Noriyuki Nomata ( Danganronpa 3: The End of Kibougamine Gakuen - Zetsubou-hen assistant director) Series Composition: Kou Shigenobu ( Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 3rd Season ) Character Design: Maki Kouno ( Bokura wa Minna Kawai-sou ), Haruna Nagata ( Kuzu no Honkai animation director) NEW , Saori Yonemoto ( Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun 2 Part 2 animation director) NEW Sound Director: Satoki Iida ( Paripi Koumei ) Studio: Lerche

The first three seasons adapting Kinugasa's school psychological light novel —also known by its short title You-Zitsu —aired in Summer 2017 , Summer 2022 , and Winter 2024 , followed by the fourth season adapting the sequel light novel in Spring 2026. Crunchyroll streamed the first season with subtitles, with Funimation streaming an English dub. Crunchyroll also simulcasted the second, third, and fourth seasons.

MF Bunko J imprint released the original light novel in 14 volumes between May 2015 and September 2019, featuring illustrations by Shunsaku Tomose ( Ange Vierge ). Kinugasa launched the 2-nensei-hen ( Year 2 ) sequel light novel in January 2020, concluding it with 15 volumes in November 2024. He subsequently began penning the 3-nensei-hen ( Year 3 ) sequel in March 2025. Kadokawa published the fifth volume on October 23.

Yuyu Ichino began drawing a manga adaptation of the first light novel in Monthly Comic Alive magazine in January 2016. Kadokawa released the 12th volume in February 2022.

Xia Sasane serialized a manga adaptation of the sequel light novel from December 2021 to December 2024. The fourth and final volume went on sale in January 2025.

A third manga adaptation subtitled 2-nensei-hen - 2nd Stage by Hachi Komada began serialization in January 2025. Kadokawa released the second volume on April 23, with the third volume scheduled for a December 22 release.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed both the light novel and manga adaptation in English in July 2018 and June 2021, respectively. The second volume of the sequel went on sale on September 1, with the third volume going on sale on December 29. The 12th and final manga volume went on sale in November 2024.

title: Classroom of the Elite Anime's 5th Season Reveals Full Title, Visual, 2027 Debut
content:
Kadokawa revealed on Sunday the title, teaser visual, teaser visual video, and 2027 debut for the fifth season of the Classroom of the Elite television anime. The title is Yōkoso Jitsuryoku Shijō Shugi no Kyōshitsu e 5th Season 2-nen Sei Hen 2 Gakki [Zen Han] (Classroom of the Elite 5th Season: Second Year, Second Semester [First Half]).

Noriyuki Nomata is returning from the fourth season to direct the fifth season at Lerche . Kou Shigenobu is also returning to oversee the series scripts. Satoki Iida is returning as the sound director. Maki Kōno is returning as character designer. Also credited as fellow character designers on the fifth season are Saori Yonemoto and Hina Nagata , who were both chief animation directors on the fourth season.

Crunchyroll streamed the season as it aired, and also streams an English dub.

The cast members from the previous seasons reprised their roles in the fourth season. The new cast for first-year students included:

• Minako Satō as Tsubasa Nanase

• Hiroya Egashira as Kazuomi Hōsen

• Momoko Seto as Ichika Amasawa

• Shinnosuke Tokudome as Takuya Yagami

• Iori Saeki as Sakurako Tsubaki

• Shōgo Sakata as Riku Utsunomiya

Noriyuki Nomata ( Kujima Utaeba Ie Hororo ) directed the fourth season at Lerche , and Kou Shigenobu ( Classroom of the Elite , Boruto: Naruto Next Generations ) was in charge of series scripts. Shigenobu also wrote the scripts with Kyōko Katsuya ( Boruto: Naruto Next Generations , Classroom of the Elite ). Maki Kōno ( The Kawai Complex Guide to Manors and Hostel Behavior ) designed the characters. Satoki Iida ( Classroom of the Elite , Amagami SS ) was the sound director. Masaru Yokoyama ( Classroom of the Elite , Freezing ) and Kana Hashiguchi ( Classroom of the Elite , Young Ladies Don't Play Fighting Games ) composed the music at Lantis .

The first season premiered in July 2017. Crunchyroll streamed the season, and Funimation streamed an English dub.

The second and third seasons adapt the original story's complete first-year-student arc. The second season premiered in July 2022. Crunchyroll streamed the season as it aired under the title Classroom of the Elite II . The third season premiered in January 2024 and aired for 13 episodes, concluding the first-year arc. Crunchyroll again streamed the season as it aired in Japan.

title: Solo Leveling’s Biggest Competitor Is Making a Huge Comeback Ahead of Anime Premiere
content:
There’s no denying that Solo Leveling is the most popular and influential webtoon and light novel series of all time. It also paved the path for the entire medium’s success across the globe, encouraging more animation studios to release webtoon adaptations. This is all thanks to the success of the anime adaptation by A-1 Pictures, as it became one of the biggest hits in history. Solo Leveling isn’t the first manhwa to get an anime adaptation, but no South Korean series pushed the medium to this level of global popularity as it did. Following the second season’s conclusion last year, the anime announced its sequel movie during this year’s Anime Expo.

However, while fans await the anime’s return, its biggest competitor is also planning a huge comeback. Along with Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint is often considered just as globally renowned. The series has already confirmed an anime adaptation in 2024, and it’s already one of the most anticipated series right now. While the anime is currently under production, the webtoon is ongoing, and it’s all set to return with its anticipated second season.

What Is the Release Date of Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint Season 2?

Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint will be released on November 24th, 2026. The official X handle of REDICE Studio only shared the Korean release date, along with a 30-second teaser. The first season of the webtoon went on a hiatus in May this year with the release of Chapter 311. The season ends on a huge cliffhanger, as it marks a major turning point in the series while stopping near the end of the Demon King Selection arc. The second season will kick off from where the story left off and wrap up the ongoing arc before moving on to the next one.

The webtoon has already adapted almost half of the web novel, so if the second season releases around the same number of chapters, then this will be the final season of the series. While the series is returning with a new season for Korean fans, the English platform Webtoon is also continuing to release the translations after several months. The serees went on a hiatus after the English release of Chapter 308 in June this year, but the next chapter was finally released on November 21st, 2026. We can expect the remaining two chapters to drop on the platform before the English debut of Season 2.

Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint Anime Hasn’t Shared Any Updates Yet

Although it’s been more than two years since the anime adaptation was announced, fans still have no idea when it will be released. Previously, the anime was expected to debut in 2027, but a report by Com2uS’ website confirmed the wait will be longer than expected. While the report shared by Com2uS stated that the anime adaptation of ORV was slated for 2028, it hasn’t been officially confirmed by major distributors or production partners, leaving its status uncertain for now.

The anime was officially announced on July 7, 2024, at the Crunchyroll Industry Panel, which means the streaming platform for the anime has already been decided. ORV is expected to be a major hit after the anime debut, especially since it shares the same system trope, similar to the beloved action series, Solo Leveling .

Are you excited for the return of the Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint webtoon? What are your expectations for the second season?

title: Mawaru Penguindrum Anime Inspires Stage Reading Production by Kunihiko Ikuhara
content:
Revolutionary Girl Utena director Kunihiko Ikuhara announced on Friday that he is writing and serving as chief director on Ikuni Produce Reading in the dark: Kodomo Broiler Sensō (Ikuni Produce Reading in the dark: Child Broiler War), a brand-new stage reading production inspired by his Penguindrum anime. The stage reading celebrates the 15th anniversary of the anime.

Akira Awano is co-writing and directing the stage reading, and Wataru Osakabe created the teaser visual and logo design. The play will run at the Shinjuku-mura Live venue in Tokyo from February 6 to February 7.

Ikuhara previously directed the "Ikuni Produce Reading in the dark Shunkin no Sasuke" play from October 31 to November 3 in 2024 at the Rikkoukai Hall. As the "Reading in the dark" part of the title indicates, this immersive form of experimental theater aims to focus on the auditory experience, by staging the production in a darkened space to remove visual cues.

The original Penguindrum anime from director Kunihiko Ikuhara ( Revolutionary Girl Utena , Yuri Kuma Arashi , several Sailor Moon television series) aired in 2011. Otome Yōkai Zakuro manga creator Lily Hoshino handled the original character designs for the 24-episode television series.

The Re:cycle of Penguindrum two-part compilation film project re-edits all 24 episodes of the television anime, but also adds new sequences and new characters. The first film, Re:cycle of Penguindrum Part 1: Your Train is the Survival Tactic , opened in April 2022. The second film, Re:cycle of Penguindrum Part 2: I Love You , opened in July 2022. HIDIVE screened the films in North America, then streamed the films along with an English dub .

title: Kurumizawa's Folly Manga Ends in 3 Chapters
content:
​

Shueisha 's MANGA Plus app publishes the series in English and describes the story:

The year is 1971 and the once popular manga artist Kurumizawa is in a major slump. The pressure builds as each new submission is rejected. But one day, he meets a young, promising artist named Hata. When he sees Hata's wonderful work, Kurumizawa hatches a dark plan...

title: 3 Female Anime Leads of 2026 Who Are Breaking the Male-Dominated Industry
content:
The anime industry has arguably long been accused of being male-dominated, largely thanks to the success of numerous shonen anime that established the boy-oriented genre as a leading force in entertainment. However, while it has taken decades longer than other mediums, the anime industry is also evolving and embracing more modern elements, including female leads taking center stage.

The year 2026 has been particularly notable in this regard, witnessing the emergence of several series featuring female leads, including masterpieces created by female authors. However, it is the female protagonists themselves who have made an epic impact, breaking the mold of a traditionally male-dominated industry. These three leads, each showcasing a different kind of strength and variety, prove just that.

3) Yamada/Tayama – Smoking Behind the Supermarket With You

Yamada from Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You is the type of lead who rarely gets the spotlight. However, this anime proves that a laid-back yet demure female protagonist can work just as well. At the supermarket, Yamada is the sweet cashier whom Sasaki puts on a pedestal. However, her alternate personality, complete with a leather jacket and piercings, showcases an unmatched sense of coolness. In both aspects, she is a character who supports the male lead through her subtle gestures. However, that doesn’t mean she exists solely for Sasaki’s sake.

Yamada’s entire character feels incredibly real, as she deals with the everyday struggles one would expect from an ordinary person. Her support for Sasaki as Tayama, and the way she receives the same support in return, create a back-and-forth dynamic that feels genuine and soothing. In essence, her role as a female lead brings a sense of realism to the anime industry and broadens its horizons in a way that is very much needed.

2) Coco – Witch Hat Atelier

The magical seinen series Witch Hat Atelier challenges the notion that magical stories featuring witches are catered exclusively towards female audiences, or that witches only exist to amplify the presence of wizards. The series does this by presenting Coco as a compelling protagonist, with her love and curiosity for magic serving as the driving force behind her journey, which is filled with darkness and obstacles. What makes Coco such a delight to watch is her unwavering resolve to never give up and overcome every challenge.

This notion was previously dominated by male protagonists in the anime industry, who constantly embodied the never-give-up spirit, while female characters were often relegated to supporting roles. However, Coco fully embodies this aspect, presenting the famous never-give-up spirit and carrying the story into a new age, arguably better than most shonen anime protagonists of 2026. In doing so, she makes one of the strongest impacts on the traditionally male-dominated industry.

1) Sitara – Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia

Women in political environments, even today in real life, are often frowned upon, and anime has followed this pattern for decades. This is what makes Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia such a refreshing series, as its entire premise revolves around a political revenge plot led by a female character, Sitara, who begins as a slave before setting her sights on the entire Mongol Empire. The series establishes this through Sitara’s experience of witnessing the death of her beloved family, who gave her everything despite their circumstances as slaves.

Swearing revenge on the Mongol Empire, whose tyranny was responsible for her family’s suffering, Sitara begins playing a political game with the aim of overthrowing the empire from within. However, that is easier said than done, and Sitara continues to face new challenges. It is astonishing to see her overcome each obstacle while remaining committed to her revenge, all while befriending another female character who becomes just as fascinating a lead as Sitara herself. Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia is truly one of the most revolutionary anime of 2026 , proving through its female leads that women can take center stage and challenge the traditionally male-dominated anime industry.

title: Yu Yu Hakusho Needs a Modern Anime Revival for One Main Reason
content:
In recent years, there’s been a massive uptick in classic anime series receiving new-and-improved reboots that aim to deliver modern animation , stories that stay more closely aligned to the story’s original source material, and even new vocal performances from legacy cast members. These successful reboots, which include the likes of Ranma 1/2 and Urusei Yatsura , are introducing an old-school style of anime to new-age fans looking to sink their teeth into a wider variety of storytelling. One of the more popular classics that’s yet to receive a proper re-adaptation is Yu Yu Hakusho , originally created by Hunter x Hunter ‘s mangaka Yoshihiro Togashi. Yu Yu Hakusho ‘s original anime adaptation from Studio Pierrot ran for 112 episodes beginning in 1992, and despite how iconic the series is, desperately deserves a fresh adaptation.

Yu Yu Hakusho follows Yusuke Urameshi, a 14-year-old delinquent who dies saving a young boy from a car accident. After being sent to the afterlife and proving his worth, Yusuke is given the chance to return back to the world of the living to work as a Spirit Detective who investigates paranormal threats and demons threatening to harm normal humans. Contrasting from other anime released during the same era, Yu Yu Hakusho stayed surprisingly close to the source material, however, the series did cut some of the manga’s earlier chapters short and expanded upon other story arcs with some additional content not present in Togashi’s original work. While there’s nothing inherently wrong with the original adaptation of Yu Yu Haksuho , the series could benefit greatly from getting a high quality reboot.

A Proper Yu Yu Hakusho Reboot Could Change Anime Forever

With the anime community’s rapid growth spurt over the last decade, new anime fans are clamoring season-to-season to find new shows to latch onto. While there have been plenty of great new ideas hitting these lineups, seeing beloved classics return with modernized animation techniques and production teams have given a number of old-school series a fresh audience to bring them back to life . Yu Yu Hakusho is the perfect show for audiences right now; the series’ focuses on themes of personal growth intertwined with the emotional and psychological cost of violence within a supernatural conflict between humans and demons.

These kinds of stories have been deeply resonating with anime fans — with similar shows like Jujutsu Kaisen becoming some of the biggest pop culture phenomenons on the planet. One of the bigger questions surrounding a re-adaptation of Yu Yu Haksuho would be what studio and directors would be capable of pulling off such a large scale project . If fans were to receive a complete remake that adapted all 19-volumes of Togashi’s original work, the show would need a production studio capable of taking on longterm productions without fear of quality dips or production stalls.

While MAPPA is a fan-favorite dream studio for imagining projects like this, other popular studios like Studio Bones, which has handled long-form shonen series like My Hero Academia and Mob Psycho 100 , or even Wit Studio, who made a name for themselves with their adaptations of Vinland Saga , Spy x Family , and Attack on Titan stand out as possible choices. That said, Yu Yu Hakusho may find a better home with Madhouse — known for their stunning adaptation of Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End , and perhaps in this particular case, for their work on 2011’s adaptation of Hunter x Hunter .

Yu Yu Hakusho Wouldn’t Be The Only Togashi Work To Retake The Global Spotlight

Yu Yu Hakusho wouldn’t be the first of Togashi’s manga to receive a reboot that makes a cultural statement for anime fans. The 2011 reboot of Togashi’s Hunter x Hunter stole anime fans from that decade and beyond’s hearts , and for good reason. The Madhouse-produced series had a 148-episode run that spanned three years, and beautifully translated Togashi’s signature illustrations to animation. Not to mention, Hunter x Hunter ‘s 2011 reboot only helped in skyrocketing the popularity of the original work more, which now has well over 100-million copies in circulation, making it one of only around twenty-five other series to reach the same level of acclaim.

While Yu Yu Hakusho is an incredible series by its own merit, having 19-collected volumes after running in Weekly Shonen Jump magazine for four years . Even years after the series came to an end, the manga reportedly has 78-million copies in circulation. Yu Yu Hakusho has consistently ranked in popularity polls around the globe like Nielsen BookScan in North America, with multiple volumes from the series ranking week-to-week. In Japan alone, Yu Yu Hakusho earned the Shogakukan Manga Award in 1993’s shonen category and ranked 17th in 2021’s TV Asahi’s Manga Sosenkyo poll wherein 150,000 manga readers voted on their top 100 series.

Needless to say, a high quality, action-packed reboot of Yu Yu Hakusho would immediately grab the attention of thousands of anime fans around the globe and dominate the anime community. Would you want to see a new version of Yu Yu Hakusho ? Let us know your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Producers Confirm These Missing Bending Styles Still Exist
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens has ended its first season without some key bending styles seen in action, and thankfully the producers behind it all teases the ones missing in action still exist in the future of the series. Avatar: Seven Havens introduced a whole new generation of the franchise with its brand new story set over two hundred years following the end of The Legend of Korr a , and that means the overall world of Bending has been changed throughout all of that time as well.

With Avatar: Seven Havens Book One coming to an end, producers Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding participated in a Reddit AMA to answer all kinds of questions fans had about the series. This included the status of whether or not Lava or Metal Bending still exists in this world that’s 200 years out from its predecessor, and thankfully it’s confirmed that they do and we still might get a chance to see those styles in action in future seasons .

Avatar: Seven Havens Producers Confirms Lava Bending & Metal Bending Still Exist

When asked about the chances of potentially seeing Lava Bending in Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ future, Spaulding confirmed that “Lava Bending has never left!” with Sethi further teasing, “You gotta keep watching!” As for the current status of Metal Bending, that had been much more in question given that one fan had noted how an Earth Bender moved the Earth under a piece of metal rather than the metal itself. But Spaulding confirmed that it still exists in the world 200 years later, but it’s just far more rare than seen in the other shows.

“Post Cataclysm, Metal Bending is an even more rare style, but it still survives,” Spaulding revealed. This did raise a lot of questions considering how Sand Bending had beens seen in Avatar: Seven Havens , and there’s still the wonder if any of the other sub-Bending categories would appear in the future . But with the producers confirming that these styles are still active even all these years in the future, it opens up the opportunity for more of that in future seasons. And that’s going to happen soon enough as more episodes are already on the way.

When Does Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 Come Out?

It’s not clear if these styles will appear as soon as Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ second season, but it’s even more likely now that Pavi has left Ellora in search of the other Havens in the future . As she unlocks more of her latent chakra powers in the coming seasons, it’s also possible that Pavi will be able to unlock all sorts of new sub-abilities too. Or meet others using these Bending styles. There might even more more sub-abilities that have yet to be seen that have developed after all this time.

Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is currently scheduled to kick off its run with Paramount+ beginning on May 21st next year with 13 episodes. They’ll be streaming with Paramount+ with a few episodes being offered each week from that point, and then will be followed by the release of Season 3 (which also has another 13 episodes) later in 2027. The series will then come to an end with its fourth season sometime after. Are you curious to see these missing Bending styles in Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ future? Let us know all of your thoughts in the comments.
